"Are you remorseful for the crime you committed?" was what Katerina Chelipova asked in a clear voice. To know more: The first Russian soldier tried in Ukraine apologizes to the widow.

16:34 Macron wants quick EU opinion on Moldova's membership application French President Emmanuel Macron today assured that he wants the European Union (EU) to give a "quick opinion" to Moldova's application to join the EU, while hosting a meeting with Moldovan President Maia Sandu in Paris. Macron added that the risk of the conflict between Ukraine and Russia spreading to other neighboring countries cannot be ruled out, whereby Moldova's integrity must be defended.

16:27 Ukraine PM and G7 finance ministers discuss steps to recover from war Ukraine's Prime Minister Denys Shmyhal said Thursday that he and Group of Seven finance ministers had discussed "practical steps to recover from the consequences of the war" in Ukraine. "Ukraine protects the entire civilized world. The support of partners will accelerate our victory," he wrote on Twitter, without giving details about the meetings. "Despite Russia's efforts to destroy our economy, together we will win!"

16:19 Russia detains deputy commander of Ukraine's nationalist Aidar Battalion Detained by Russia the deputy commander of a unit that belonged to Ukraine's nationalist Aidar Battalion, Denis Muryga, before it was reorganized and absorbed into the Ukrainian Army, Russian media reported. A Rostov-on-Don court today issued a two-month remand for the serviceman, according to the Interfax agency. According to this source, Muryga, who has Russian and Ukrainian citizenship, was detained while trying to cross the border with Russia in April as a suspected refugee in the Rostov region.

16:10 NATO wants to address Turkey's "concerns" about Sweden and Finland NATO wants to address the "concerns" raised by Turkey to block the membership applications of Sweden and Finland. NATO Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg said so today. "Of course, we want to respond to the concerns that Turkey has expressed" to find an "agreement to move forward," the alliance chief declared in Copenhagen, reaffirming his "confidence" in a "quick decision" to welcome the two Nordic countries. Stoltenberg defended that "it is not unusual for NATO to have different opinions on important decisions" and he is confident of overcoming the differences.

16:01 ???? Russia says Ukrainians in areas controlled by its military have a say over their future Russia has said it will be up to residents of areas in Ukraine controlled by Russian troops to determine their future status. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said today that people living in those places should "determine how and with whom they want to live." During a conference call with reporters, the official was answering a question about some Russian officials who said the country might make moves to incorporate the captured Kherson region in southern Ukraine.

15:53 Filmmaker Serebrennikov defends that Russian culture "has always promoted humanist values" Russian filmmaker and dissident Kirill Serebrennikov on Thursday in Cannes rejected the boycott of Russian culture, although he said he understood those who call for it, during the third day of the competition, where he is competing for the Palme d'Or with "Tchaikovsky's wife". "The boycott of Russian culture is unbearable to me because Russian culture has always promoted human values, compassion," he said at a press conference on his first visit to the festival after he managed to leave his country on March 28. To know more: Serébrennikov: "I find the boycott of Russian culture unbearable". Astrid Meseguer, special correspondent in Cannes, reports.

15:44 Sanchez supports the struggle for democracy of the Belarusian opposition leader The President of the Government of Spain, Pedro Sanchez, on Thursday conveyed to the Belarusian opposition leader in exile, Svetlana Tikhanovskaya, Spain's support for her work in favor of democracy in her country, at an international moment marked by the war in Ukraine and the role of that country. The President of the Spanish Government received Tikhanovskaya today, Thursday, at the Moncloa Palace. The two interlocutors held a meeting in which they analyzed the situation in Belarus, as well as the evolution of the war in Ukraine after Russia's invasion.

15:34 Erdogan reinforces Turkey's no to Sweden and Finland to join NATO Turkey's veto of Sweden and Finland's entry into NATO is becoming increasingly clear, and on Thursday Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan accused Sweden of being "a nest of terrorists". This is how Erdogan expressed himself, outraged by the asylum given from Stockholm to militants of the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) and also to the fugitives of Fethullah Gülen's brotherhood both there and in Finland. For the Turkish president "there is no place for terrorists in a security organization", so he considers that neither of the two countries meets the requirements to join the alliance, in addition to remarking that he does not want to break his relations "neither with Putin, nor with Zelenski", as Ankara is the mediator between Russia and Ukraine.

15:25 Red Cross rushes to register as prisoners of war Ukrainian soldiers surrendered in Mariupol The International Committee of the Red Cross already has hundreds of prisoners of war registered as such after they surrendered from their defense of the Azovstal steelworks in Mariupol. This status ensures respect for international humanitarian law during conflicts and requires a registration process that included obtaining basic personal data of the soldiers. No figures have been given from Kyiv on the mass surrender of Ukrainian fighters that is taking place in the last hours in Mariupol, but it is known that there are still several thousands locked up in the manufacturing plant

15:16 Russian soldier on trial for war crimes in Ukraine apologizes to widow of man he killed "I know you will not be able to forgive me, but I ask for your forgiveness." So apologized the first Russian soldier tried in Ukraine for having committed war crimes during the invasion of the country. He is Sergeant Vadim Shishimarin, 21, who is in Kyiv in custody after admitting that he killed a 62-year-old unarmed man while pushing his bicycle in a village in northeastern Ukraine. "Tell me, please, why did you come, to protect us, from whom, from my husband whom you killed?" the widow of the deceased asked him, who finally got no answer from the young Russian serviceman

15:07 Almost 90% of Spaniards believe that Vladimir Putin should be pressured to withdraw from Ukraine The latest barometer of the Center for Sociological Research (CSIC) has revealed that almost 90% of Spaniards surveyed are in favor of putting international pressure on the Russian president, Vladimir Putin, to withdraw troops from Ukraine. On the other hand, almost 80% of those asked agree with sending arms, ammunition and all kinds of military equipment to Ukraine from NATO with the aim of defending itself against the Russian invasion. However, the percentage plummets to 43.9% when asked whether NATO would have to intervene militarily to support Ukraine and go to war with Russia.

14:57 Russia will defend its "stolen" assets in Ukraine Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov has assured that following the invasion of Ukraine, Russian authorities will defend assets arrested in the country to prevent Russian assets from being "stolen" as elsewhere. "Our reaction is negative, we are going to fight against it, we are going to defend our assets," Peskov has declared after it became known that Ukraine has seized Russian and Belarusian assets worth about $1 billion. In this regard, Peskov believes that it is "the continuation surely of the line that has become fashionable lately in a number of states, which is, in fact, a line to steal other people's assets."

14:48 Russia has been preparing in recent months for a food crisis Russian presidential adviser Maxim Oreshkin revealed Thursday that Russia has been preparing for months for a possible food crisis in the country in the face of the avalanche of international sanctions that are sapping the economy. Specifically, he dates to the end of 2021 the beginning of the Kremlin's operations to avoid a food shortage in the face of the blockade to its export capacity of its substantial wheat and fertilizers to grow crops. In this regard, Oreshkin has assured that "the main cause of the world hunger that will take place this year is the ill-considered economic measures of the United States and the European Union".

14:38 Military experts assure that the majority of Russian soldiers killed in Ukraine are ethnic minorities, poor and young people The number of Russian soldiers killed in the war in Ukraine remains a big unknown for the whole world, since Moscow puts the number of soldiers killed in combat at about 1,351, while Kyiv multiplies this figure almost tenfold. Even so, what is becoming increasingly clear is that the profile of the Russian fighter fallen in the invasion of Ukraine is mainly from the south of Russia, in the Muslim region of the North Caucasus and Siberia. It is also noted that the average age of the deceased is between 21 and 23 years old, although many of them were not even in their twenties when they were killed during the war in Ukraine. In addition, they also have in common a low purchasing power, in the absence of more reliable data from independent international organizations

14:29 Spain reduces gas imports from Russia to less than 8% The Spanish energy system is becoming more and more independent from Russia, according to the Secretary of State for Energy, Sara Aagesen, who reported that Russian gas now accounts for less than 8% of the total consumed in our country. On the other hand, Qatar has been identified as the supplier most capable of exporting gas to Spain in the coming years through investments that would make it a key partner in the short and medium term. Unlike countries in Eastern Europe, Spain has "very little" dependence on Russian gas, which is "easily substitutable" thanks to the country's gas pipeline and the six regasification plants located in the country

14:17 The EU is considering the creation of an international tribunal to judge the war crimes of the Russian army in Ukraine The European Parliament has initiated proceedings to propose the creation of an international tribunal dedicated to judge the "crime of aggression perpetrated against Ukraine by the political leaders and military commanders of Russia and its allies". From Brussels they consider it necessary to establish judges dedicated to the conflict, since the International Criminal Court has no jurisdiction over Russia and Ukraine, because neither of them is in the Rome Statute. In addition, they consider it essential to take into account that "due to the current hostilities, there is a serious risk that evidence of war crimes will be destroyed and cannot be safely collected and preserved for the purpose of investigating war crimes in Ukraine."

14:11 Ukraine still does not report how many soldiers have surrendered to Russia at the Azovstal steel plant As fighters are leaving the Azovstal steel plant in Mariupol, huge figures are coming in on the number of soldiers who were defending the manufacturing plant, a total of 1,730 according to the Russian Defense Ministry, a figure not yet confirmed by Kyiv. The Ukrainian side has only hinted that there will be an exchange of prisoners with Moscow, but no information has been given on the numbers, which suggest a much larger contingent of troops than initially expected. Moreover, according to the leader of the self-proclaimed Donetsk People's Republic, Denis Pushilin, "as of today more than half of them, this is absolutely accurate, have already left there with a white flag", so there are still many others: "Let them surrender, let them live, let them honestly face the charges for all their crimes", Pushilin asked.

14:02 Turkey stops Sweden and Finland from joining NATO The accession of Sweden and Finland to NATO, which took its first step yesterday with the presentation of their candidatures, continues to be debated and blocked by Turkey, from where they regret that their security concerns are not "listened to". The envoys of La Vanguardia in Brussels and Istanbul, Esther Herrera and Jordi Joan Baños, have picked up the strong position of Ankara against the entry of Finland and Sweden to NATO as long as they give asylum to militants of the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK), with which the Turkish government is at war. On the other hand, the relationship between Russian President Vladimir Putin and his Turkish counterpart Recep Tayyip Erdogan is also not an obstacle to be ignored in the complex process of the Nordic countries' entry into the alliance.

13:53 EU removes tariffs on Ukrainian products for one year The European Parliament has voted by a large majority to suspend import duties on all products coming from Ukraine for one year, so they will be able to reach the European Union without tariffs. According to Latvian People's MEP Sandra Kalniete, "giving Ukraine the support it needs to defend itself does not end on the battlefield, it includes ensuring that the Ukrainian economy remains resilient and competitive". The vote went through with 515 votes in favor, with 32 against and 11 abstentions and will liberalize trade with Ukraine, which sells more than 40% of its goods to the EU

13:43 Russia will not unblock Ukrainian ports to let out the accumulated wheat International pressure for the distribution of wheat and grain from the ports of Ukraine, one of the world's major food exporters, is not having an effect in Russia, where they assure that they will maintain the blockade of Ukrainian ports. At least this will be the case as long as international sanctions are maintained, as the Russian Foreign Ministry warned on Thursday in response to the UN request to avoid a food crisis. The Kremlin is calling for the suspension of the international community's punishments, which are stifling the Russian economy due to the war in Ukraine, so that ships can start sailing to the whole world with wheat.

13:34 EU allows member states to buy gas from Russia, but asks that it not be in rubles Brussels has ruled on the possibility of European Union member states buying Russian gas and has given the green light for them to do so, but has recommended against transactions in rubles. Despite the sanctions packages that the EU has been launching against Russia and its policy of seeking energy independence from Moscow, in the last few hours it has given a respite to those countries most in need of Russian imports. EU representatives have commented that as long as they pay in the currency of their current contracts and declare compliance with the obligations of these agreements, member states are free to buy Russian gas, despite the war in Ukraine

13:26 Erdogan declares Sweden "a nest of terrorists" and rules out allowing it to join NATO Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan said Thursday that "Sweden is a nest of terrorists" and that "there is no place for terrorists in a security organization," referring to the Nordic country's request to join NATO. This was Erdogan's strong message to Stockholm, which he accuses of giving asylum to militants of the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK), at war with the Turkish government, and also to the fugitives of Fethullah Gülen's brotherhood. "We have already explained our 'no' to Finland and Sweden to our friends and we will continue to do so," has insisted Erdogan, increasingly opposed to the accession of the new countries to the alliance. In addition, the Turkish leader has recalled the "mistake" that Ankara made according to Erdogan by allowing Greece to join NATO instead of using its veto right

13:16 More than 700 Ukrainian fighters surrender at Azovstal steel mill The Russian Defense Ministry has reported that 771 Ukrainian soldiers have laid down their weapons at the Azovstal steel mill in Mariupol to surrender to the invading troops, as reported by theGeneral Igor Konashenkov. In fact, Moscow estimates that 1,730 Ukrainian fighters have stopped fighting to resist in the steel plant, where they have been practically incommunicado for several weeks and under constant siege by the Russian army. For the surrendered, Konashenkov has guaranteed that "all those who need hospital treatment receive assistance in medical institutions" and have moved to Novoazovsk, in the Donetsk region

13:07 ???? The return of hundreds of refugees to Ukraine, a report by Rosa M. Bosch "Shortly after the war broke out in Ukraine, Alyona Ostashevska, an English teacher, her son Andrii, 17, and daughter Anna, 14, left their home in Kyiv, terrified by bombs. At the beginning of March, they were already settled in an apartment in Reus, altruistically lent by its owners. But the need to be close to her husband, a police officer, and to facilitate Andrii's access to university prompted Alyona to return home." Like Alyona and her son Andrii, thousands of Ukrainian refugees have had to return to their country at war with Russia since the beginning of this year forced by necessity, despite worldwide announcements of welcoming them with open arms, Rosa M. Bosch tells us in her report. "Yes, we know that some refugees have left or want to leave, they are the ones coming from Kyiv and western Ukraine, but the government warns that it is still dangerous to return," comments Olha Dzyuban, a member of one of the largest Ukrainian communities in Catalonia. Figures show that there are currently more than 21,000 Ukrainians living in hotels, relatives' homes and communal accommodation in Catalonia, and some 7,000 health cards have been issued

12:58 Russia expels five Portuguese diplomats and declares them persona non grata The Russian Foreign Ministry announced a few moments ago that it has decided to expel five Portuguese diplomats from the country after Lisbon did the same with ten workers of the Russian embassy in Portugal. The Kremlin regrets that "this unfriendly step will reflect negatively on Russian-Portuguese relations" and reiterates the "strong protest" against the initial expulsion ordered by the Portuguese government. There have already been more than 420 diplomats expelled from Russia so far this year, a record considering that in the last two decades that figure was not exceeded, although these actions are clearly linked to the war in Ukraine

12:49 ????? ' Europe, Europe', the analysis of the continent convulsed by the war in Ukraine "What are we talking about when we talk about Europe? Again that question with as many answers as there are interlocutors. If only it were as easy as drawing an equal sign in mathematics. Answers, moreover, fleeting, because they soon cease to be valid. Europe as a cursed puzzle, as a well-intentioned projection, abyss and paradise in the same space, solution and problem, model and counter-example". Marta Rebón reviews in La Vanguardia the complicated dynamics that have transformed Europe and how the old continent is responding to the war in Ukraine initiated by a Russia increasingly distanced from the West. It is even more difficult to define and analyze what we call Eastern Europe, a "terra incognita", as defined by Rebón in his article, where he gives a glimpse of a possible rapprochement between the countries in the area and the West.

12:40 Russia could resume negotiations with Ukraine, according to its deputy foreign minister The peace negotiations between Russia and Ukraine, interrupted in the last hours after having broken off, could be resumed if Kyiv shows willingness to dialogue with Moscow. This was assured by the Russian Deputy Foreign Minister, Andrei Rudenko, who guaranteed that "as soon as they express their willingness to return to the negotiating table, we will naturally respond in the affirmative". On the other hand, Rudenko defended the actions of the negotiators sent by the Kremlin: "It was not us who interrupted the negotiation process, it was our Ukrainian partners who paused it". In contrast, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov acknowledged that "the talks are in fact not progressing" and stressed that there is "a complete lack of desire on the part of the Ukrainian negotiators to continue this process."

12:31 "I ask for forgiveness": the first Russian soldier tried in Ukraine for war crimes apologizes to the country Russian non-commissioned officer Vadim Chichimarine, on trial in Ukraine for committing war crimes during the first days of the invasion of the country, has asked for "forgiveness" for his actions in the northeast of the country. "I know you will not be able to forgive me, but I ask for your forgiveness," said the 21-year-old serviceman, who admitted killing a 62-year-old man during his operations on February 28.Chichimarine spoke to Katerina Chelipova, the widow of the civilian killed by the Russian soldier, who was the first since the war began in Ukraine to be tried by Kyiv

12:23 Voices critical of Russia's invasion of Ukraine begin to emerge from Russia Gonzalo Aragonés tells us from Moscow how for the first time since the war in Ukraine began, opinions are beginning to be heard that are dissonant with the overwhelming majority of the media that support President Vladimir Putin. The latest case has been that of retired Colonel Mikhail Khodarionok, who has predicted a Russian military disaster in Ukraine, as the "special military operation" launched by the Kremlin earlier this year is progressing. Khodarionok came clean, asserting that Russia is "in geopolitical solitude" having invaded its neighboring country, with words that have shaken the media establishment for the honesty of the respected colonel

12:14 Italy seeks to avoid a world food crisis by unblocking Ukrainian ports The international alert for the shortage of wheat and other cereals that the world will face in the coming days due to the blockade of Ukrainian ports dedicated to their export has been answered on Thursday by the Italian Prime Minister, Mario Draghi, who has proposed an international action to solve the dangerous dynamics. As reported by our correspondent in Rome, Anna Buj, Draghi intends to implement his proposal to remove the mines installed by the Russian army at the exit of Ukrainian ports. Draghi himself explains that "it is necessary that the ships carrying this wheat can pass and if the ports have been mined by the Ukrainian army, they should be demined for this purpose". For this reason, the Italian leader believes that "all the parties involved should open at this time a parenthesis of collaboration to avoid a humanitarian crisis that would cause millions and millions of people to die in the poorest parts of the world".

12:03 NATO asks to take into account the importance of morale in the war in Ukraine The chairman of NATO's Military Committee, Rob Bauer, has exposed that the war in Ukraine has shown that one should never "underestimate" the importance of the morale of the troops and "know what you are fighting for". On the other hand, he assured that in recent months the Alliance has shown itself capable of adapting its military posture. In this way, he pointed out that "a new era" has begun for the transatlantic organization and that Russian President Vladimir Putin's war in Ukraine has presented NATO with "a new strategic dilemma and reality".

11:51 West urges Russia to facilitate Ukrainian grain exports Ukrainian grain exports, virtually paralyzed by the Black Sea naval blockade, so the UN, the United States and other countries have called on Russia to return to normal. "It is estimated that right now there are 22 million tons of grain in silos in Ukraine that could immediately help those in need if they could be taken out of the country," explained the U.S. Secretary of State, Antony Blinken. For its part, the UN has been warning since the beginning of the conflict of the enormous impact of the conflict on food security, given that Ukraine and Russia are two of the world's main cereal producers. The organization's Secretary General, António Guterres, has confirmed that he is in contact with Russia, Ukraine, Turkey, the United States, the European Union and other key countries to try to reach an agreement that would allow both the outflow of Ukrainian grain and unimpeded sales of Russian food and fertilizers.

11:39 Russia will send oil rejected by Europe to Asia and other regions Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak has explained that Russia will send oil rejected by European countries to Asia and other regions. He also points out that Europe will have to find alternative supplies that will be more expensive. Western sanctions imposed on Russia after its troops entered Ukraine in February forced several oil buyers to delay or refuse shipments, which in turn dented Russian oil production. Novak said Russian oil production fell by about 1 million barrels per day in April, but has risen by 200,000 to 300,000 barrels per day in May, with more volumes expected to be restored next month.

11:28 Uncertainty over the fate of the 1,000 evacuees from Azovstal Following the surrender of Ukrainian troops at the Azovstal metallurgical complex in Mariupol, there is great uncertainty over the fate and final destiny of the 959 servicemen evacuated by the Russian army. The resistance in Azovstal, the last stronghold in Ukrainian hands in the city of Mariupol, ended this Tuesday, when the Ukrainian Ministry of Defense determined that the soldiers should survive because they had "fulfilled their mission Members of the Duma, the lower house of the Russian Parliament, requested that they should not be exchanged with Russian soldiers taken prisoner by the Ukrainians, although the Kyiv Government, which at first assured that they had agreed to the exchange of prisoners and even that they had "Putin's personal word" for it.

11:15 Scholz reiterates that supplying arms to Ukraine is not an escalation of the situation German Chancellor Olaf Scholz insisted Thursday that there will be no peace dictated by Russia and stressed that supplying arms to Ukraine is not an escalation of the situation, but a contribution to repel Russian aggression. "Putin, still continues to think that he can dictate peace by bombing, but he is wrong, as he was already wrong about the decision of the Ukrainians and the unity of our alliances," he stressed. In this way, he assures that everything Europe is doing: sanctions against Russia, the reception of millions of refugees in the European Union, humanitarian and economic support to Ukraine and also the supply of armaments, including heavy equipment, is aimed at preventing Russia from winning the war. Moreover, noting that "rarely before has the Atlantic Alliance been so alive and so essential as it is today", he thanked US President Joe Biden for his great contribution.

11:06 The surrender of Azovstal allows Russia to redeploy part of its troops on other fronts With the fall of the Azovstal steelworks in Mariupol, the Russians have now conquered the entire line linking the annexed Crimean peninsula with the separatist regions of the Donbas and have begun to redeploy part of their troops on other fronts. Despite this new Russian advance, the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine maintains that in the last hours the Russian army is not achieving in the last hours its military objectives, especially in the east of the country. On his side, the President of Ukraine, Volodymir Zelensky, has signed a decree to extend the martial law and the deadline for general mobilization, while he assured that "Kherson, Melitopol, Berdyansk, Enerhodar, Mariupol and all our cities and communities which are under occupation, under temporary occupation, must know that Ukraine will return".

10:54 Erdogan's toll on NATO Turkey has reiterated its refusal of Sweden and Finland's accession to NATO, causing member countries to be unable to start accession discussions. From the Atlantic Alliance, therefore, it is feared that the blockade will be prolonged and derail the urgent procedure that the United States in particular had envisaged for these new partners. For his part, Erdogan is confident that the United States will intervene on his country's behalf in other matters of interest and unblock the situation before the NATO summit in Madrid.Esther Herrera reports from Brussels and Jordi Joan Baños from Istanbul.

10:45 Ukraine puts the number of children killed since the start of the war with Russia at more than 230 Ukrainian authorities on Thursday raised the number of children killed since the start of the Russian military offensive to more than 230. "These figures are not final, as the work is ongoing in places of active hostilities and in the temporarily occupied and liberated territories," he added. He also stressed that Donetsk oblast has the highest number of casualties, with 144 dead and wounded. Behind are the Kiev region with 116, the Kharkov region with 100, the Chernobyl region with 68, the Kherson region with 48, the Lugansk region with 47 and the Mikolayev region with 44.

10:33 G7 discusses today financial assistance to Ukraine German Finance Minister Christian Lindner has exposed that this Thursday that G7 countries are going to discuss giving financial assistance to Ukraine. "Ukraine stands for our values and therefore we have a responsibility to help it financially," he said, although he refused to confirm the aid figures of 15 billion euros that has been published in some media. Finance ministers and central bank governors from the G7 - Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the UK and the US - are meeting today and Friday in Königswinter in western Germany.

10:24 U.S. announces €205 billion in food assistance for Ukraine New U.S. aid package to the Russia-Ukraine conflict, with the transfer of €205 billion as part of the global supply chain crisis, which may push 40 million people worldwide into extreme poverty and food insecurity this year. In addition, U.S. Secretary of State Antony Blinken is confident that the U.S. Congress will "very soon" approve approximately $5.5 billion---5.243 billion euros--"in additional funding for humanitarian assistance and security." Blinken has also urged governments around the world and international organizations to "compel" Russia to create humanitarian corridors so that food and other vital supplies can safely leave Ukraine by land or sea.

10:13 Surprise in Russia over several criticisms of Ukraine campaign The head of Chechnya, Ramzan Kadyrov, and retired Colonel Mikhail Khodarionok, have in recent hours taken issue with several of the moves Russia has made in the invasion of Russia. Kadyrov assures that Russia has made specific "mistakes" and "errors" shortly after the beginning of the conflict, although he points out that "we are fulfilling the plan, the task that the president set us, we are fulfilling one hundred percent". For his part, Khodarionok states that "although we do not want to admit it, we are in geopolitical solitude" Gonzalo Aragonés, correspondent in Moscow, reports.

10:01 Gazprom says it continues to supply gas to Europe Russian gas producer Gazprom says it continues to supply gas to Europe via Ukraine through the Sudzha entry point, with volumes on Thursday seen at 63.3 million cubic meters (mcm), up from 51.6 mcm on Wednesday. According to Gazprom, Ukraine rejected a request for gas supplies through the main Sokhranivka entry point.

09:52 Ukraine claims that the Russian military is not achieving its military objectives The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine claims that Russia is failing in recent hours to achieve its military objectives, especially in the east of the country, in the Donetsk region, where it is now focusing its offensive. "The Russian occupation forces undertook offensive and assault operations on four eastern fronts and were unsuccessful", they assure. They also warn that the "Russian command" acting in the occupied areas in the pro-Russian region of Donetsk plans to mobilize university students to participate in the combat, due to the lack of other reservists.

09:40 Biden to sign additional $100 million in Ukraine security assistance U.S. President Joe Biden may sign $100 million in military aid to Ukraine today, Thursday, including additional artillery munitions and counter-artillery battery radars. It is a new request as part of a series of transfers to help Kyiv repel the invasion ofRussia, according to two informed sources

09:40 Call between U.S. and Russian Chiefs of General Staff on Ukraine Russia's Chief of the General Staff Valery Gerasimov and Chairman of the U.S. Joint Chiefs of Staff Gen. Mark Milley held a phone call, RIA news agency has reported Thursday, citing the Russian Defense Ministry. They discussed issues of "mutual interest," including Ukraine, the cited agency said. The call came six days after a telephone conversation between the two countries' defense ministers, the first since Russia launched what it calls its special military operation in Ukraine.

09:39 One civilian killed in Russia's Kursk region The governor of that Russian federate entity, Roman Starovoit, reports that a Ukrainian attack on a border town in Russia's Kursk region has resulted in the death of at least one civilian and several wounded. "The new attack perpetrated by the enemy early this morning against Tiótkino unfortunately ended in a tragedy. At the moment it is known that there is at least one dead among the civilian population," the governor wrote. Tiótkino, a town of about 3,000 inhabitants, is located in the far west of the Kursk region, on the border with the Ukrainian region of Sumy, which was the scene of fierce fighting in the first weeks of the so-called "special military operation" launched by Russia in Ukraine last February 24.

09:27 More than half of Azovstal fighters have left the steel plant The resistance at the Azovstal steel plant in Mariupol is on its last legs and more than half of the Ukrainian fighters inside the steel plant, Russian news agency TASS reports citing the leader of pro-Russian separatists controlling the area, Denis Pushilin. However, Ukraine and Russia have given conflicting versions on the number of fighters who have left the plant.

09:18 Michel assures that Putin has already lost the Ukrainian war The President of the European Council, Charles Michel, has assured that the President of Russia, Vladimir Putin, is already "the loser" of the war against Ukraine because he has been wrong on issues such as the capacity of the Russian army or the reaction of unity on the part of the European Union. "Vladimir Putin is already the loser of this war," Michel declared during the plenary session of the European Economic and Social Committee. Michel stressed that the Kremlin has been wrong about "its own military capabilities, about the Ukrainian resistance force, about determination and about European unity". The President of the European Council pointed out that Putin has managed to "wake up NATO, which will undoubtedly expand soon", referring to the foreseeable entry of Sweden and Finland.

09:10 G7 finance ministers want to help Ukraine financially The finance ministers of the G7 countries, the most industrialized in the world, want to help Ukraine financially to ensure its ability to pay in the wake of the direct consequences of the war in Ukraine. Germany's Finance Minister, the liberal Christian Lindner, said today, Thursday, that his country will help Ukraine with 1 billion euros after deliberating with his G7 counterparts at the Petersberg Hotel in Königswinter, outside Bonn.

09:06 Mariupol City Council points to possible serious toxic spill due to shelling The ongoing Russian shelling of the Azovstal steelworks in Mariupol, southern Ukraine, may have led to a leakage of hydrogen sulfide into the Sea of Azov, a highly polluting substance. The Mariupol City Council warns that "a leakage of this liquid will completely kill the flora and fauna of the Azov Sea. In addition, these hazardous substances can reach the Black and Mediterranean Seas". For his part, the mayor of Mariupol, Vadym Boichenko, announced the need for the immediate entry of international and UN experts into the steelworks facilities to study the situation and prevent a global environmental disaster. The port city of Mariupol has suffered the heaviest shelling since the Russian invasion began on February 24, and has been practically destroyed, while the few remaining citizens are facing a serious humanitarian crisis due to the shortage of drinking water and food.

08:53 Zelenski extends martial law and general mobilization deadline Ukrainian President Volodymir Zelenski has signed a decree to extend martial law and the deadline for general mobilization in the country in view of the possibility of a prolonged war with Russia. "We are obliged to expel the occupants and ensure the real security of Ukraine", Zelenski has expressed in his usual morning message. On the other hand, he affirmed that Russia is still looking for a "wonderful" and final weapon that will achieve its goals, something that shows "the total failure of this operation and (Moscow's) fear of admitting mistakes". He also promised that "Kherson, Melitopol, Berdyansk, Enerhodar, Mariupol and all our cities and communities that are under occupation, under temporary occupation, should know that Ukraine will return".

08:40 Ukrainian refugees undertake return due to lack of opportunities The Russian invasion of Ukrainian territory has caused millions of people to leave the country fleeing the war. However, the lack of opportunities has prompted several of them to make the journey back to Ukraine or to nearby countries such as Poland or Hungary. Journalist Rosa M. Bosch reports on the situation of Alyona Ostashevska, an English teacher, her son Andrii, 17, and her daughter Anna, 14.

08:29 Amnesty International calls on Russia to "respect rights" of Azovstal POWs Amnesty International has called on Russia to "respect the rights" of Ukrainian prisoners of war who surrendered in the siege of the Azovstal steel mill. The soldiers deployed in the port city of Mariupol have been "dehumanized" by the media and portrayed in Russian propaganda as neo-Nazis, said the NGO's deputy director for Eastern Europe, Denis Krivosheev. "This characterization raises concerns about their fate as prisoners of war," Krivosheev said in a statement. Amnesty International has already documented summary executions of captives in eastern Ukraine at the hands of pro-Russian separatists, as well as the killing of civilians by Russian soldiers in recent weeks, the organization noted.

08:18 UN downgrades its global growth forecast for this year to 3.1% The UN has downgraded its growth forecast for the world economy this year from the initial 4% to 3.1% as a result of the war in Ukraine. In a revision of its economic outlook report, the UN estimates that the world's major economies will be clearly affected by the conflict and will progress below expectations. Furthermore, it forecasts that Ukraine's economy will sink by 2022 by 30% to 50% as a result of the war. For its part, Russia will shrink by 10.6% due to the harsh sanctions imposed on it in response to the invasion of the neighboring country.

08:05 The European Commission proposes to invest 500 million euros in military armament On the other hand, the European Commission has proposed to invest 500 million euros until 2024 to acquire military armament needed by the countries of the European Union in the short term. A report prepared by the EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs, Josep Borrell, and the EC, has highlighted shortcomings in the European defense industrial and technological base and proposes measures in two tranches, in the short and medium-long term, to remedy them. "The massive delivery of arms to Ukraine has led to a lack of capabilities in Europe," EU sources have stressed.

07:53 The European Union allocates 248 million euros for taking in refugees Ukraine On Wednesday the European Commission confirmed that Poland, Romania, Hungary, Slovakia and the Czech Republic will receive 248 million euros, to support reception and border management systems. In addition to assisting in the management of external borders this emergency aid, to be financed from Interior funds, will serve to provide those fleeing the Russian invasion with immediate assistance, such as food, transport and temporary accommodation. The countries that will receive these funds are the European Union member states that have taken in the largest number of refugees arriving from Ukraine since the war began.

07:40 Russian soldiers killed in Ukraine: young, poor and from ethnic minorities Although the Kremlin is keeping the number of losses secret, most of the thousands of Russian soldiers who have died in Ukraine are very young, from the poorest regions of their country and often from its ethnic minorities, experts say. The Kremlin has offered no information on the matter since last March 25, a month and a day after the start of the war. By then, some 1,351 of its soldiers had fallen in battle.

07:31 NATO cannot move forward with Sweden and Finland's membership NATO has announced that it has been unable to move forward immediately with the Swedish and Finnish membership process in the wake of Turkey's President Rece Tayyip Erdogan deploying an extensive list of grievances. Only after all NATO allies give their consent will Sweden and Finland be able to start their membership in the organization.

07:22 Italy calls for ceasefire after Russia's expulsion of 24 of its diplomats Following the decision to expel 24 diplomats, Italy has called for "an immediate ceasefire" that "guarantees the start of negotiations." In a terse statement, Foreign Affairs has assured to "take note of the decision of the Russian Federation to expel 24 members of the Italian diplomatic and consular missions" and added that its personnel "have always performed their duties in full respect of the Vienna Convention on diplomatic relations". After learning of Moscow's decision, Italian Prime Minister Mario Draghi said that diplomatic relations and channels with Russia should not be interrupted under any circumstances.

07:13 Expulsion of French and Italian diplomats As well as the 27 diplomats expelled from the Spanish Embassy in Moscow and the Consulate General in St. Petersburg, Russia has also taken a similar decision with French and Italians. Thus 34 French diplomats were expelled in response to the same measure taken by Paris in April against 41 Russian diplomats stationed in France. Moscow also announced today the expulsion of another 24 Italian diplomats.

07:00 Baltic MPs call for prompt and determined action against Russia The chairmen of the foreign affairs committees in the parliaments of Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia have raised the importance of acting together "promptly and with determination" against Russia to curb its expansionist ambitions and prevent its disinformation campaigns from succeeding. The Estonian parliamentarian, Marlo Minkelson, stated that 70 percent of the Ukrainian population is asking to join NATO and "we must give them the category of candidate country because they deserve to be admitted because they are fighting for their freedom, if not for everyone's freedom". For her part, the representative of the Lithuanian Parliament, Liucija Laima Andrikiene, assured that the next NATO summit in Madrid should serve for the organization to rethink its policy of deterrence and defense, since the territories claimed by Russia "must be defended and also recovered".

06:51 First Russian soldier on trial in Ukraine pleads guilty to killing civilian Ukraine on Wednesday began the first trial of a Russian soldier for allegedly committing war crimes since the Russian invasion on February 24. In this the first session of the trial, the defendant, Vadim Shishimarin, pleaded guilty to killing an unarmed civilian. The 21-year-old sergeant Shishimarin faces 10 to 15 years in prison or life imprisonment if convicted on the charges against him: violation of the laws of war in combination with premeditated murder.

06:42 Kremlin continues to fail to disclose whether it will agree to prisoner exchange Following the withdrawal of nearly 1,000 Ukrainian defenders who have left the Azovstal plant in Mariupol, the Kremlin continues to fail to disclose whether it will agree to prisoner exchange as proposed by Kyiv in the face of growing rejection among the political elite at home and pro-Russian leaders in the Donbass. Russia claimed yesterday that another 694 Ukrainian defenders of the metallurgy "had surrendered", including 29 wounded. Russia has not disclosed whether it will agree to a swap, but within the country there have already been harsh voices in the lower house, the Prosecutor's Office and in the pro-Russian Donbass strongly rejecting this possibility.

06:30 Russia calls on the southern Ukrainian town of Melitopol to join "the Russian family " Russian Deputy Prime Minister Marat Jusnulin has called on the southern Ukrainian town of Melitopol to join "the Russian family" during a visit to areas controlled by Russian forces. "The future of this city is to work within the framework of the Russian family. That is why I have come here, to offer maximum support, the possibility of integration," he said. The Russian politician visited the city of about 160,000 people that was seized two days after the start of the Russian military campaign in Ukraine.

06:19 Turkey blocks Sweden and Finland's accession to NATO Turkey is not in favor of Sweden and Finland's accession to NATO. Moments after the accession application was submitted, the Ottoman country has officially made it known that it was not prepared to accept the entry of the Nordic countries if its concerns are not "listened to". It is not the first time that Istanbul has spoken of conditions for accepting Sweden and Finland into the Alliance, in particular its request that they end their policy of tolerance towards members of the Kurdish political exile, in particular the PKK (the Kurdistan Workers' Party). Esther Herrera reports from Brussels.

06:10 Finland and Sweden formalize their NATO membership application The Swedish and Finnish ambassadors to NATO handed in their NATO membership application on Wednesday at NATO headquarters, where they met with NATO Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg, who said "this is a good day at a critical moment for our security". Stoltenberg said that NATO allies "are determined to resolve all issues and reach rapid conclusions". NATO is relying on a rapid entry process given the threat from Russia, although the process usually takes between eight and 12 months.

06:01 Russia expels 27 Spanish diplomats Last April 5, the Spanish Executive expelled 27 people from the Russian embassy in Madrid among diplomats and other staff. This Wednesday, therefore, Russia has responded with the expulsion of 27 diplomats from Spain The Spanish Foreign Ministry rejects the measure taken by the Russian Government but will not take any decision in response, at least for the time being.

05:56 Russia digs in and prepares for a long war Ukrainian Defense Minister Oleksiy Reznikov has assured that "Russia is preparing for a long military campaign. In the Kherson and Zaporiyia regions the Russian occupants are building fortifications to go on the defensive in case of necessity". In the same speech, the Defense Minister called "not to allow Russia to prolong this conflict" as a prolonged campaign "carries the risk of a global food crisis and a new migration crisis".

05:50 Ukrainian surrender at Azovstal steel mill (Mariupol) After many days of defense, Ukraine has finally surrendered at the Azovstal steel mill in an attempt to maintain its control. In a first step, 265 men, 51 of them seriously wounded, were evacuated since Monday night in buses identified with the letter Z, as hated in Ukraine as praised by many in Russia, where there is talk of surrender. To know more: The last fighters of Azovstal, in Mariupol, surrender to the Russian forces. Catalina Gomez Angel reports from Dnipro, Ukraine.
