title: [Live] "Missile attacks on Kiev," official officials report.
text:
A night view of Kiev after the mayor declared a curfew between 10 p. m. and 7 a. m. on February 24, 2022. In the early hours of the 25th, loud explosions were reported near the Ukrainian capital.Photo: Pierre CromInrecent hours, tensions around Ukraine rose after Vladimir Putin ordered "military action" in the Donbas. Western leaders, such as Joe Biden, Boris Johnson and Olaf Scholz, condemned what happened, while warning that they will take action in response to what they consider "an unjustified attack". Meanwhile, explosions are reported from several Ukrainian cities and the country warns that it was attacked by Russian troops from Belarus. We tell you, minute by minute, what is happening in these tensions

.???????????? Before we begin, a bit of context: for weeks, Russia has deployed some 150,000 troops on the border with Ukraine and on Monday recognized the independence of two separatist territories: Donetsk and Lugansk. This stoked accusations that the Kremlin is preparing a large-scale attack against the neighboring country

.???????????? And a summary of what happened in the week:

On Tuesday, Germany suspended authorization of Nord Stream 2.On the same day, the Russian Senate authorized sending soldiers to separatist enclaves: The vote formally allowed Putin to send troops to the Donbas region of Ukraine.At the same time, the United States mobilized more troops to Eastern Europe.On Wednesday, the European Union formally announced sanctions on Russian leaders, as well as on banks and the defense sector. While Ukraine (prior to the Russian military action) announced a plan to mobilize its reservists and urged its citizens to leave Russia.Biden also announced sanctions against Russia on Wednesday: This first round of sanctions will prevent Russia from raising Western funds to repay sovereign debt. The US also said it would sanction the company in charge of operating the Nord Stream 2 pipeline.Yesterday, Ukraine declared a state of national emergency, while neighboring countries are preparing for a possible migration wave. About 5 million people could be displaced, according to U.S. data.Russia also said on Wednesday that separatist regions in eastern Ukraine asked it for military backing. Hours later, Reuters reported that five explosions were heard in the city of Donetsk, while the U.S. said a full-scale invasion was imminent.10:40 p.m.: Border unit in Zaporizhia region targeted by missile attackTheUkrainian border post in Zaporizhzhya region was hit by a missile attack, the Ukrainian Border Guard Service reported. The attack, according to the announcement, occurred at 4:25 a. m. (Ukrainian local time) at the Primorsky Pasad border unit in the Zaporizhia region. According to reports, there are dead and wounded.

10:33 p.m.: Videos show explosion south of KievAlarge explosion occurred in the sky over the southern outskirts of Kiev, the New York Times reports. Witnesses filmed burning debris falling over parts of the city. The videos appeared to show at least two surface-to-air missiles fired from the Ukrainian capital before the explosion.

10:14 p.m.: Russian plane shot down over KievTheUkrainian Interior Ministry said a Russian plane was shot down over Kiev. As read in The Guardian, Anton Gerashchenko , an adviser to Ukraine's interior minister, added a series of photos to his Telegram account, including what he said was a nine-story residential building on fire.

10:10 p.m.: Chinese embassy in Ukraine seeks to evacuate its citizensThediplomatic entity is organizing charter flights for Chinese citizens seeking to evacuate. There are about 6,000 Chinese citizens in Ukraine. The announcement came after a Chinese Foreign Ministry spokeswoman refused to call Russia's attack on Ukraine an "invasion," reports The New York Times.

9:57 p.m.: Loud explosions heard in Ukraine's capitalTwoloud explosions rang out early Friday (local Ukrainian time) in central Kiev on the second day of Russia's invasion of Ukraine, an AFP reporter noted

."Attacks on Kiev with cruise or ballistic missiles resumed. I heard two loud explosions," Ukrainian Deputy Interior Minister Anton Herashchenko said on his Telegram account.

Meanwhile, Ukraine's armed forces confirmed that additional weapons are being brought to Kiev, amid reports of explosions in the Ukrainian capital.

The press that is in Ukraine also reported that the explosions were heard. This was reported by The Guardian reporter Emma Graham Harrison.

9:00 p.m.: The European Union announces the approval of another package of "massive and targeted sanctions" against RussiaThiswasannounced by the President of the European Commission, Ursula von der Leyen, who assured, via Twitter, that "the approved package shows how united the European Union is". This package aims to affect the following areas:

Financial sanctions, targeting 70% of the Russian banking market and key state-owned enterprises, including in defense.Energy sector, a key economic area that particularly benefits the Russian state. The export ban will affect the oil sector, making it impossible for Russia to upgrade its refineries.Aviation, as the sale of aircraft and equipment to Russian airlines is prohibited. In addition, Russia's access to crucial technology, such as semiconductors or state-of-the-art software, is being limited.Visas: diplomats and related groups and businessmen will no longer have privileged access to the European Union."8:18 p. m.: New Zealand, Russia and Japan announce sanctions againstRussiaAustralia

's Prime Minister Scott Morrison said he will impose more sanctions on the Russians. "Australia will impose further sanctions on the oligarchs, whose economic clout is of strategic importance in masking members of the Russian parliament who voted to authorize the use of Russian troops in Ukraine to invade it. We are also working with the United States to align with its new sanctions on television commercials, which are key accomplices in the aggressions."

For her part, New Zealand Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern called for the immediate withdrawal of Russian forces in Ukraine, announced a travel ban for Russian officials and added that she is considering expelling the Russian ambassador. "New Zealand calls on Russia to do the right thing and immediately cease military operations in Ukraine, and withdraw permanently to avoid catastrophic and pointless loss of innocent lives," she said.

Meanwhile, Japan said it plans to limit semiconductor exports to Russia, while freezing the assets of some individuals and groups linked to Russia, and will stop issuing visas to certain Russians.

8:00 p.m.: Russian forces close in on Kiev, Ukrainian capitalAccording toThe New York Times, by the end of the first day of the invasion, Russian special forces and airborne troops were advancing toward the outskirts of Kiev. While it is not known exactly what Putin's ultimate goal is, U.S. officials believe that it may be to impose the replacement of President Volodymyr Zelensky's government. Meanwhile, Ukrainians continue to move toward the western side of the country.

6:50 p.m.: WhiteHouse White Housepress secretary Jen Psaki told a news conference that there are credible reports that personnel

at theChernobylfacility are being held hostage.

This illegal and dangerous hostage-taking, which could disrupt the routine civil service efforts needed to maintain and protect the waste facilities nu6

:00 p. .m: Volodimir Zelenski, president of Ukraine, gives a report on those killed in the Russian invasion"137 heroes, our citizens," lost their lives, Zelenski said in a video posted on the government's website, adding that 316 other Ukrainians were injured during the clashes

.In his remarks, he added: "I don't see anyone" to fight alongside Ukraine.

5:39 p.m.: Ukraine decrees general mobilization over Russia'sinvasionThrough the official account of the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine it was made known that in connection "with the military aggression of the Russian Federation against Ukraine, and in order to ensure the defense of the state, maintain combat readiness and mobilization of the Armed Forces of Ukraine and other military formations, a general mobilization is announced."

The decree published on the website of Volodimir Zelenski, president of Ukraine, says the measure will affect persons subject to "compulsory military service and reservists" and will be in effect for 90 days in all regions of Ukraine.

5:00 p.m.: Ukrainians take shelter, as aggressions continueTheGuardian reports that aggressions continue in Ukraine. For example, it is known that throughout the night (local time) a battle took place in the Ukrainian city of Sumy.

Meanwhile, images of residents taking shelter in Kiev and Kharkiv metro stations are circulating on social networks, as reported by Benoît Vitkine, a reporter for the French newspaper Le Monde.

4:30 p.m.: UN Security Council to vote on condemnation of RussiaTheUN resolution, which is in the hands of the 15-member Security Council, would condemn, "in the strongest possible terms, Russia's aggression, invasion and violation of Ukraine's sovereignty," a U.S. official said. It also "reaffirms Ukraine's sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity. And it requires the Russian Federation to withdraw its forces immediately, completely and unconditionally." A European diplomat at the UN also said the resolution would declare that "Russia can no longer encroach on its neighbors."

The New York Times reads that the resolution is likely to have more symbolic, than real, power, but the U.S. and its allies have said that the U.N. and the council have a responsibility to act, and that a Russian veto would only demonstrate the country's isolation.

4:15 p.m.: Emmanuel Macron talks with Vladimir PutinTheFrench president spoke with his Russian counterpart, the Kremlin reported. The two had "a serious and frank exchange" on Ukraine, and Putin "gave a thorough explanation of the reasons and circumstances" surrounding the invasion, the statement issued from Moscow read.

"After speaking with the Ukrainian president, and in coordination with him, Macron called Vladimir Putin to demand an immediate end to the military operations," the French leader's office reported. In that dialogue, Macron reminded Putin that Russia was now exposed to "massive sanctions" by the European Union.

Macron is the fourth leader with whom Vladimir Putin has met after the attack on Ukraine, as in previous hours the Russian leader held meetings with the Prime Minister of Pakistan and with the leaders of Iran and India.

4:00 p.m.: UN warns of Ukrainians fleeing after invasionAbout100,000 people fled their homes in Ukraine and thousands sought refuge abroad after the Russian invasion, the UN said. "We think about 100,000 people fled their homes already and may have been displaced inside the country and that several thousand crossed international borders," Shabia Mantoo, a spokesman for the UN High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), told AFP.

3:47 p.m.: Explosions and a preliminary toll of wounded and dead reported from Ukraine"The Ukrainian city of Mariupol is under heavy fire with reports of hundreds of explosions. The city is one of the largest Ukrainian ports on the Sea of Azov. Taking Mariupol would help Russia secure a direct land route to Crimea, the Ukrainian peninsula annexed by Russia in 2014," so reports Kyiv Post on social media.

Journalists also reported additional explosions from the direction of Ukraine's Hostomel airport. "Big explosion from the direction of Hostomel airport just now. Bigger than the previous ones. One explosion, not several," reported reporter Jane Lytvynenko.

Ukrainian Health Minister Oleh Lyashko reported that 57 people were killed and 169 injured. In addition, the deputy defense minister added that heavy shelling is still going on in the eastern Donetsk region.

3:28 p.m.: European Union warns of "massive and severe" sanctions against RussiaTheleaders of the 27 countries of the European Union agreed that "sanctions will cover Russia's financial, energy and transport sectors", according to the Declaration issued after the summit held in Brussels. The measures, which are not yet known in detail, contemplate export controls, visa issuance and the inclusion of Russian officials on the sanctioned list.

3:00 p.m.: IMF and World Bank warn about the consequences of the war in UkraineClarifyingthat they will offer assistance to Ukraine, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank (WB) warned about the repercussions that the Russian aggression in Ukraine may have on the global economy

.IMF head Kristalina Georgieva said she was "deeply concerned" about the consequences of the fighting in Ukraine and warned in a tweet that the conflict "adds significant economic risk for the region and the world." As read by AFP, the IMF is in the process of disbursing $2.2 billion in assistance to Ukraine under a loan program that will end in June.

For his part, David Malpass, president of the WB, noted that "the institution "is preparing options for major support to the people of Ukraine and the region, including immediate budget support."

2:52 p. m.: The Inter-American Court of Human Rights speaks of the central role of international lawThisis the call that the entity made from social networks: "The role of public international law is central and today's events demonstrate it. I make a special call to solve this conflict based on the law and the application of basic principles, such as that a State must respect the sovereignty of another."

2:00 p.m.: Joe Biden ends his official statement after Russian aggression in UkraineAssertingthat what is happening today is the greatest threat to Europe and the world, and reaffirming that Ukraine has been an independent country for thirty years, the U.S. president said that the sanctions interposed by the allies show the union of almost two thirds of the countries in the world. "We are not doing this alone. We represent half of the world's economy."

The U.S. president also added that, in coordination with his allies, "we will limit Russian business in dollars, pounds and euros. We are attacking their finance, technology and industrial capabilities. The sanctions, he said, are intended to have "severe consequences" on the Russian economy in the long term.

According to Reuters, Biden assured that Putin would be a pariah on the international stage and that his actions would cost Russian civilians dearly.

Biden added: "Putin has much bigger ambitions than Ukraine. He wants, in fact, to re-establish the old Soviet Union. That's what this is all about and I think his ambitions are completely contrary to where the rest of the world has come."

1:31 p.m.: Germany says Putin "will try to wipe Ukraine off the map "Olaf Scholz, Germany's chancellor, said that "we are witnessing the start of a war of a magnitude that we have not seen in Europe in more than 75 years" since the end of World War II. "This is an attempt to change with the use of force the borders in Europe, perhaps even to wipe an entire country off the map."

12:52 p.m.: Russians call first day of invasion a "success"All operations assigned to the groups of troops of the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation for the day were successfully completed," said Defense Ministry spokesman Igor Konashenkov

.Thus, Russia said its military achieved its objectives on the first day of the invasion of Ukraine, despite warnings of harsh sanctions from Western countries.

12:35 p.m.: Russian forces reportedly seized Chernobyl"After heavy fighting in the Chernobyl area, Russian troops took control of the nuclear power plant in

the

area.trying to take Chernobyl. Our soldiers are sacrificing their lives so that the tragedy of 1986 will not happen again. This is a declaration of war against the whole of Europe".12:15 p. ...: Ukraine announced a toll of dead and wounded in the south of the country.At least 13 Ukrainian civilians and nine Ukrainian servicemen were killed on Thursday in the Kherson region (southern Ukraine), which is currently under partial control of Russian troops who invaded the country, regional authorities reported.

"Thirteen civilians, including two children, were killed and nine soldiers were killed in the attack on the Kherson region," the local government specified on Facebook. The town of Guenichesk was seized by the Russians, it added.

12:10 p.m.: Boris Johnson unveils new package of sanctions against RussiaThe prime minister said the UK is announcing the biggest sanctions package Russia has ever seen, which includes the following measures:

Russian banks will be excluded from the UK financial system.Russian state-owned and private companies will be banned from raising money in the UK.The amount of money Russians can hold in British bank accounts will be limited.Sanctions will also apply to Belarus.Aeroflot will be banned in the UK.Export controls, similar to those imposed by the United States, will be implemented, meaning a ban on items such as semiconductors and other high-tech equipment.The export of dual-use items to Russia, which could eventually be used militarily, will also be banned.Before the House of Commons, Johnson described Putin as a "bloodied aggressor who believes in imperial conquest, always determined to attack his neighbor, no matter what we did." He added that "Putin will stand condemned in the eyes of the world and in the eyes of history. He will never be able to wipe the blood of Ukraine from his hands."

12:00 p.m.: Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan meets Putin.He is the first leader to meet with the Russian president after the attack on Ukraine. Khan arrived in Moscow yesterday on a two-day trip, amid rising tensions between the two countries, but when the military action had not yet taken place.

Some read this visit as "ill-timed". As read in The Guardian, Michael Kugelman of the Wilson Center in the United States said: "There is a risk that Khan's visit to Moscow will be perceived by many in the West as an indirect endorsement of Putin's decree on eastern Ukraine, a move that much of the world has condemned and that Pakistan itself is unlikely to support. Although Khan's visit was planned weeks ago and focuses on bilateral relations, the timing is striking and presents some problems of optics."

11:42 a.m.: G7 ready to act if invasion causes "disruption" to energy supplies"We are closely monitoring global oil and gas market conditions," the G7 said in a statement following a video conference to discuss the crisis sparked by the invasion.

The group said it supports "consistent and constructive engagements and coordination between major energy producers and consumers in the collective interest of a stable global energy supply."

11:27 a.m.: 'This is a threat to the global order': G7The G7, which groups advanced economies, on Thursday condemned the Russian invasion of Ukraine and assured that the attack constitutes "a serious threat to the international order, with ramifications beyond Europe." Russian President Vladimir Putin "has placed himself on the wrong side of history," the G7 said in a statement following a meeting to discuss the crisis.

11:22 a.m.: Russian forces seize a military airport near Kiev.Russian forces seized Thursday a military airport about forty kilometers from Kiev, the capital of Ukraine, said Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, who assured that the operation to recover it was already underway.

According to Zelenski, who was speaking in a video address, the incursion of Russian paratroopers in Gostomel, where the airport is located, was "blocked" and the Ukrainian forces "received the order to annihilate them".

10:20 a.m.: Curfew declared in KievKiev Mayor Vitaly Klitschko announced Thursday a curfew to protect the safety of the capital's residents. "The curfew will last from 10 p.m. to 7:00 a.m.″, he added in a statement, specifying that public transport will not operate at those times but that metro stations will remain open to serve as a shelter in case of attacks.

10:09 a.m.: Fighting at Ukraine's Chernobyl power stationUkrainian authorities reported fighting near the nuclear waste repository.

According to an advisor to the Ukrainian Interior Ministry, Anton Guerashtshenko, the "occupants' troops entered from Belarus into the area of the Chernobyl power plant." "Members of the National Guard protecting the depot put up stubborn resistance," he said on the Telegram messaging network.

???????? 9:55 a.m.: Biden to meet with G7.U.S. President Joe Biden will brief the United States on the situation in Ukraine and next steps. According to him, this crisis will cause a "catastrophic loss of lives".

In a few moments, they will hold a virtual meeting with the leaders of the G7 (United Kingdom, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States). Prior to the appointment, Biden "convened a meeting of the National Security Council (...) to address the latest developments in Ukraine," the White House reported.

"The United States and its allies and partners will respond in a united and determined manner. The world will hold Russia accountable," Biden said in his first, after Russian missiles began falling on Ukraine. Biden also spoke by phone with his Ukrainian counterpart, Volodimir Zelenski, and said he had pledged to "provide support and assistance to Ukraine and the Ukrainian people."

9:28 a.m.: Fighting erupts at military base near KievThe Ukrainian military announced Thursday that there was fighting with Russian troops near Kiev for control of the Gostomel military airport.

"There is ongoing fighting for control of the Gostomel airport," located a few kilometers northwest of Kiev, Valery Zaloujnyi, speaking on behalf of the Ukrainian armed forces, announced in a message on Facebook. AFP reporters saw helicopters flying at low altitude towards the city from the north.

8:46 a.m.: Russian authorities threaten those taking part in protests.The Russian Interior Ministry, the Prosecutor's Office and the Russian Investigative Committee warned their population against any protest actions. The Committee noted that people who take part in rallies about "the tense situation in foreign policy" or in clashes face prosecution.

Journalist Kevin Rothrock tweeted some images of the protests in Moscow. "They are arrested almost immediately, often as they leave their homes," Rothrock wrote.

8:32 a.m.: Four missiles were fired from Belarus.The Armed Forces of Ukraine reported that four ballistic missiles were fired from the territory of Belarus in the southwestern direction.

7:53 a.m.: 'Russia is invading on multiple fronts': former Ukrainian ministerAndriy Zagorodnyuk, Ukraine's former defense minister, told The Guardian that there are ground invasions on several fronts in the country. "They are quite close to the city of Kherson now. The situation is really critical there. They are also trying to surround Kharkiv. It seems that Kharkiv at the moment is the main target. They are also trying to get to Kiev using a battlefield group. The group left Belarus and was stopped," Zagorodnyuk commented.

???????? 7:33 a.m.: Ukrainian military plane crashes near KievA Ukrainian military plane crashed Thursday near Kiev with 14 people on board, the state emergency situations service announced. The plane went down near the village of Trypillia, about 50 kilometers south of the Ukrainian capital, according to the same source.

???????? 6:55 a.m. 6:55 a.m. Russian forces arrive in the Kiev region: border guardsRussian troops crossed the Vilcha border point in the Kiev region, 50 kilometers from the border with Belarus, the Ukrainian Border Guard Service reported today. "Russian troops violated the state border. The enemy's war equipment crossed through the Vilcha border point, about 150 kilometers north of the capital," the entity reported according to which the Ukrainian Army planted battle with the Russian Army.

6:39 a.m.: NATO activates defense plansThe North Atlantic Treaty Organization countries agreed to activate their defense plans, following Russia's offensive in Ukraine, announced Thursday the secretary general of the military alliance, Jens Stoltenberg. During a press conference in Brussels, the official also confirmed that the transatlantic military alliance will hold a leaders' summit on Friday via videoconference in the wake of the invasion of Ukraine.

6:29 a.m.: Multiple explosions were heard in Kiev."Confirmed by Ukrainian authorities. A large air assault operation with Mi-8 helicopters at Antonov International Airport in Hostomel. Interior Ministry says Russia has taken control. Very dangerous; it's just 15 minutes west of a highway from the capital," wrote BuzzFeed correspondent Christioher Miller.

6:10 a.m.: Ukraine asks Turkey to close Russian access to the BosphorusUkraine asked Turkey to close the Bosphorus straits to Russian warships, which use the passages to enter the Black Sea, The Guardian reported. "We conveyed our official request to the Turkish side regarding the closure of the airspace, the Dardanelles and of the Bosporus for Russian ships," Ukraine's ambassador to Ankara, Vasyl Bodnar, said, according to Turkish media Hurriyet. Bodnar added that Ukraine is also asking Turkey to sanction Russian businesses.

???? 5:30 a.m.: NATO allies invoke Article 4."Today we have held consultations under Article 4 of the Washington Treaty. We have decided, in accordance with our defensive planning to protect all Allies, to take additional measures to further strengthen deterrence and defense throughout the Alliance. Our measures are and will remain pre-emptive, proportionate, but not escalatory," the North Atlantic Council said in a statement.

4:59 a.m.: Separatists in eastern Ukraine are taking control of territories: RussiaThe Russian military announced Thursday that pro-Russian separatists in eastern Ukraine were making territorial gains against the Ukrainian army.

General Igor Konashenkov, a spokesman for the Russian Defense Ministry, said in television remarks that the rebels advanced three kilometers in the Donetsk region and one and a half kilometers in Lugansk, and assured that civilians had "nothing to fear" because Russia has military targets.

title: Summary: What is going on between Russia and Ukraine?
text:
Russian President Vladimir Putin began the invasion of Ukraine early Thursday morning with shelling and ground incursions by Russian troops in several parts of the country, including near the capital Kiev, which have already caused dozens of deaths. The start of the invasion has generated a barrage of international condemnations and reactions. Some 27 members of the European Union will meet this Thursday and announce new sanctions to pressure and isolate Moscow. For its part, NATO is planning a meeting by videoconference this Friday. For its part, the United States will submit this Thursday a draft resolution to the UN Security Council to condemn Russia for this "war".

 Putin, who for weeks had deployed more than 150,000 military personnel on the borders with Ukraine, crossed a point of no return on Thursday at dawn.

"I have taken the decision for a military operation", declared the President, three days after having recognized the independence of the separatist regions of eastern Ukraine and having obtained the legal framework from the Parliament for a military intervention. Putin assured that he was not seeking "occupation", but "demilitarization and denazification" of Ukraine and to defend pro-Russian rebels in the east of the country. Shortly after his speech explosions began to be heard in several Ukrainian cities, from Kiev to Kharkov, its second city on the border with Russia, but also in Odessa or Mariupol, on the shores of the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov. The Russian army assured that it destroyed 74 Ukrainian military installations, including 11 airfields, and the separatists in eastern Ukraine are advancing and taking control of territories.In Moscow, the Kremlin spokesman, Dmitri Peskov, affirmed that the offensive will last as long as necessary, depending on its "results" and considered that the majority of Russians will support it.

Why did the operation take place? After decades of tensions between the neighboring countries, which increased in the last weeks due to the presence of troops near the Ukrainian border and the practice of missiles inside Russia, the President of this country, Vladimir Putin, ordered a special military operation on Ukrainian territory. The reason is that the Ukrainian territories of Donetsk and Lugansk have declared that they want their independence from the country and consider themselves pro-Russian, so Putin, the President of Russia, recognized them as independent republics and sent troops to their territory on a peaceful mission. Because of this, the Russian Army now has the green light to be in these two regions of the Donbas, where these rebel republics of Ukraine are located, however, the arrival of the troops has been seen as an invasion, which has already caused deaths and structural damage to the territory. Ukrainian President Volodimir Zelenski on Wednesday called for security guarantees from Western countries and Moscow."Ukraine needs clear and concrete security guarantees, immediately," from both Western countries and Russia, Zelenski told a press conference. "I think Russia should be among the countries that give us those guarantees," he insisted, recalling that he had proposed on several occasions to meet with his counterpart Vladimir Putin to seek solutions to this crisis.The Ukrainian president thanked his Polish and Lithuanian counterparts for their support and for deliveries of weapons and military equipment."We are united in the conviction that the future of European security is decided at this moment at our home, in Ukraine," Zelenski said.

First casualties In Ukraine, the authorities broke off diplomatic relations with Moscow, compared Putin's Russia to Nazi Germany and vowed to defend themselves, while calling for international help to force Moscow to respect the peace.The government announced that more than 40 Ukrainian soldiers and a dozen Ukrainian civilians were killed. In addition, 18 people were killed in a shelling of a military base in a town near the Ukrainian port of Odessa, local authorities reported.Ukrainian border guards also admitted that Russian troops penetrated from Belarus, in a region 150 kilometers north of Kiev, to carry out a Grad missile attack on military targets.There were also other ground incursions from the south in the Crimean peninsula, annexed by Moscow in 2014. Belarus, a Kremlin ally, assured it was not participating in the offensive.Ukrainian President Volodimir Zelenski announced martial law throughout the country, but asked the population not to panic.The president also raised the specter of World War II by comparing the invasion suffered by his country with the 1941 Nazi offensive against Ukraine, then part of the Soviet Union."The Ukrainian forces are fighting fierce battles. The enemy has suffered heavy losses which will be even heavier," he guaranteed, promising to "inflict maximum casualties" on the aggressor.The Ukrainian army claimed to have killed 50 Russian occupants and shot down five planes and a helicopter in the east of the country. All these casualty reports are so far impossible to verify with independent sources.The Ukrainian authorities also closed the airspace to civil aviation for security reasons, while Russia shut down shipping in the Sea of Azov, which connects the two countries.

The global economy The situation on the Ukrainian border worsened last week, with violence escalating in the east of the country, the scene of a war since 2014 between the Ukrainian army and pro-Russian separatists that has left more than 14,000 dead.On Monday, after recognizing the independence of the separatist "republics" of Donetsk and Lugansk, Putin questioned the very legitimacy of Ukraine's existence. A day later, the Russian Parliament gave the green light for the deployment of Russian forces in Ukraine.The invasion has hit international markets. Brent crude oil topped $100 per barrel for the first time in seven years and stock markets around the world plummeted on Thursday. The Moscow Stock Exchange, which halted trading for a few hours, suffered losses of more than 30% and the Russian currency, the ruble, hit an all-time low against the dollar before Russia's central bankintervened.

Fleeing the war Russia assured that civilians in Ukraine "have nothing to fear", however, in Kiev hundreds of people rushed to the subway to seek shelter or a way out of the city."I woke up to the sound of bombs, packed my bags and fled," said Maria Kashkoska, 29, in a state of shock in the subway.In the middle of the night, traffic in the capital was typical of rush hour. Vehicles full of families were seeking to get out of the city, westward, as far as possible from the Russian border 400 km away.On the roads of eastern Ukraine, the army was omnipresent. A spokesman for the Civil Defense indicated that civilians were being evacuated, but that these operations were disrupted by gunfire and poor communications.Colombians in Ukraine have reported that mobility is reduced, as many inhabitants of the city look for ways to leave to take shelter from the impending conflict.

title: UPDATE 3-Russia ramps up aid to banks,  forex  market after invasion of Ukraine
text:
* Russian rouble, assets in free-fall after Putin orders troops into Ukraine

* Russian c.bank intervenes on forex market for first time since 2014

* Offers extra forex and rouble liquidity for banks

* Finmin stops new OFZ bonds offering for the upcoming weeks

* Stress-tests show financial market, top companies ready for sanctions, finmin says (Adds details, quotes, background, releads)

By Elena Fabrichnaya and Katya Golubkova

MOSCOW, Feb 24 (Reuters) - The Russian central bank beefed up the banking sector with extra liquidity and started to sell foreign currency on the forex market after the rouble fell to all-time lows on the day Moscow sent its troops into Ukraine.

After weeks of denying plans to attack neighbouring Ukraine, Russian forces fired missiles at several cities in Ukraine and landed troops on its coast on Thursday.

The United States promised harsh sanctions, covering everything from Russia's top banks' operations with dollars to the energy sector should Moscow invade its neighbour.

And as Russia's currency, bonds and stocks all tanked, the central bank intervened on the forex market for the first time since 2014, when Russia annexed the Crimea peninsula from Ukraine.

It was not immediately clear how much forex the central bank was selling but the rouble pared some losses and moved away from an all-time low of 89.60 against the dollar and a crucial threshold of 100 versus the euro it was approaching in the morning.

"The military operation in Ukraine makes harsh sanctions unavoidable," Raiffeisenbank said in a note. "The rouble crash was stopped by the central bank's interventions but its potential for further weakening remains high."

The regulator might have spent between $1 billion and $2 billion to support the rouble on Thursday, according to Promsvyazbank analysts. The central bank is due to disclose the sum on Monday.

It also nearly doubled daily dollar offers under forex swap operations with banks to $5 billion, provided another 874 billion roubles ($10 billion) at a daily repo auction and expanded collateral options for its funds to secure its 300 lenders with additional funds.

As a precaution before the sanctions, Russian lenders brought $5 billion in foreign exchange bank notes to the country in December and increased liquidity coverage of their foreign exchange assets last month.

State-owned Sberbank and VTB both said their operations continued as usual on Thursday, but the latter urged its corporate clients to refrain from dollar and euro transactions.

A number of Muscovites experienced troubles in withdrawing dollars and euros from ATMs in the centre of the city, and a cash machine in Moscow's northeast stopped operating after a Reuters witness withdrew 20,000 roubles.

But no big ATM queues were seen in Moscow on Thursday.

GOVERNMENT PLEDGES CONTROL

While Russian officials say that Moscow's financial shield is strong enough to withstand both the volatility and sanctions, new curbs would "weaken Russia's economic base and its capacity to modernise", European Commission chief Ursula von der Leyen said.

Russia ran a historic high current account surplus of $120.3 billion last year, its gold and forex reserves stand at a record $643 billion and debt-to-GDP level is below 20%.

"Russia has financial resources enough to maintain the financial system in the light of sanctions and external threats," the government said on Thursday, adding that the budget has over 4.5 trillion roubles in available extra funds.

The government drew up specific plans after conducting stress-tests to assess possible sanctions, saying in the statement that the "financial market and largest companies are fully ready to implement them". It did not provide details.

But a Moscow real estate company urged its staff in an email marked 'IMPORTANT' on Thursday to use cards connected to the domestic MIR payment system, set up as an alternative to the western Visa and MasterCard payment systems after 2014.

"We recommend all our staff members to move their salary payments to the cards using this payment system," the letter seen by Reuters said, adding that a decision to open such cards in Sberbank, VTB and AlfaBank should be taken by the end of the day. title: Russia Attack Roils Markets; Defense Stocks Rally -- WSJ
text:
By Caitlin Ostroff, Anna Hirtenstein and Quentin Webb 

Investors rushed for safety, pushing down stocks and lifting the prices of oil, gold and government bonds, after Russian missiles and airstrikes hit Ukraine's capital, Kyiv, and more than a dozen other cities across the country.

Futures tied to the S&P 500, Nasdaq-100 and Dow Jones Industrial Average fell between 2.5% and 3%. The S&P 500 reached correction territory earlier in the week, and futures are indicating the Dow is on track to do the same. Nasdaq futures are pointing to the index approaching a bear market.

The Russian attack -- swiftly condemned by President Biden -- heightens the pressure on a global economy already reeling from snarled supply chains and some of the highest inflation in years, with Europe likely to bear the brunt of the economic impact.

"This is what appeared unbelievable to most investors, and this is actually happening," said Slava Smolyaninov, Moscow-based chief strategist at BCS Global Markets. "It's a complete change of everything; we are in a different world right now."

The pan-continental Stoxx Europe 600 fell over 3%. The MOEX benchmark for Russian stocks tumbled 30%, putting it on course for its biggest drop on record. Asian stock indexes also fell sharply, with Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index dropping over 3%, and Japan's Nikkei Stock Average closing at its lowest since November 2020.

The Russian ruble weakened to a record low, declining as much as 9% against the dollar and trading at 90 rubles to $1, before recovering moderately. The Russian central bank said it would intervene in the foreign-exchange market and banned short selling.

Ukraine's foreign-exchange market suspended its operations under martial law measures, according to a statement from its central bank. The country's stock exchange also said it was postponing activity.

Brent crude oil, the global benchmark, topped $100 a barrel for the first time since 2014, with the front-month contract rising 8.4% to $104.94. Prices for its U.S. equivalent, West Texas Intermediate, also jumped.

Other commodities markets also convulsed. Natural-gas futures in Europe surged 31% and benchmark prices for aluminum and nickel, two metals for which Russia is a major producer, rose to their highest levels in about a decade. Wheat and corn futures also advanced to multiyear highs, since both Russia and Ukraine are major grain producers.

"We thought Putin's strategy was largely around negotiation; this was the consensus among investors. We haven't had any serious military conflict in Europe for a very long time so there's no playbook for this, " said Gregory Perdon, chief investment officer at Arbuthnot Latham. "A lot has changed since last night."

Gold and U.S. Treasury bonds, which both typically rally in times of stress, rose in price. The most actively traded gold futures contract added 3.3%, to about $1,973 a troy ounce, the highest level since September 2020.

The yield on the benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury note declined to 1.858% from 1.976% on Wednesday. Bond yields fall as prices rise. European government bonds also rallied, with the equivalent German bund yield falling as low as 0.111%.

The dollar strengthened, with the WSJ Dollar Index gaining 0.8%. Currencies considered to be havens, such as the Japanese yen, also appreciated, while cryptocurrencies tumbled, with bitcoin falling nearly 7% to about $35,000.

Investors are building up their cash buffers due to the market stress, said Florian Ielpo, head of macro at Lombard Odier Investment Managers. The funds he manages currently hold the most cash since the market crash in March 2020.

The invasion reverberated in markets in Eastern Europe and Turkey. The Polish zloty and the Hungarian forint both depreciated 2.5% against the dollar. The Turkish lira fell 3.7%. Polish bank stocks tumbled, with PKO Bank Polski falling 13.5%. Wizz Air, an airline with its key markets in Eastern Europe, declined over 11%.

Shares of other European companies with sizable operations in Russia also plunged. Austria's Raiffeisen Bank, which had over 20% of its workforce in Russia at the end of 2021, declined 17%. UniCredit fell 9% and Société Générale slid 11.5%. French car maker Renault, which also has a large Russian subsidiary, fell nearly 10%.

Defense stocks rallied, with BAE Systems rising 5.4%. U.S.-listed Northrop Grumman climbed 8.8% and Lockheed Martin added 3.4% in premarket trading.

The Russian attack comes at a time where volatility in markets was heightened, due to looming changes in Federal Reserve monetary policy.

"The game-changer for me is, what does this mean for the Fed? Ultimately now, interest rate hikes and aggressive tightening are going to be very difficult," Mr. Perdon said.

Amid the chaos, Chinese e-commerce giant Alibaba and vaccine-maker Moderna are expected to post earnings ahead of the opening bell. Beyond Meat, Etsy and cryptocurrency exchange Coinbase are scheduled to report after markets close.

The latest data on U.S. weekly jobless claims are expected at 8:30 a.m. ET. Economists expect the number to edge down amid the tight labor market, after it rose unexpectedly last week.

-- Megumi Fujikawa and William Horner contributed to this article.

title: Russia attacks Ukraine: Minute by minute after Russian invasion
text:
Russia today launched a military operation against Ukraine, with the alleged aim of pacifying the armed conflict that has been taking place in eastern Ukraine since 2014. This is the minute by minute of everything that has happened in the country. All updates in Central European Time (CET).

13:41 Russia nips anti-war demonstration attempts in the bud.

"I was detained when I was leaving home," activist Marina Litvinovich, who had called for a protest after learning about the Russian military operation in Ukraine, wrote on Telegram. She confirmed her detention by police in a message to Reuters. Litvinovich had called on Russians to gather in protest in several Russian cities tonight.

13:31 UNHCR calls for keeping borders open for refugees.

UN High Commissioner for RefugeesFilippo Grandi called on countries neighboring Ukraine to "keep their borders open to those seeking safety and protection," after Ukrainian citizens have already sought refuge in territories such as Romania, Hungary or Slovakia.

"There are no winners in a war, but countless lives will be shattered," the head of the UN Refugee Agency (UNHCR) said in a statement and called for respect for both civilian lives and non-military infrastructure.

13:18 "It is an attack on democracy and freedom in the world".

British Prime Minister Boris Johnson said that the Russian offensive "is not just an attack on Ukraine, but on democracy and freedom in Eastern Europe and around the world." In a message to the nation, Johnson promised a "huge package of sanctions" and added that "diplomatically, politically, economically and militarily, this horrific and barbaric action by Putin must end in failure."

13:09 Russian troops cross the border in the Kiev region.

Russian troops crossed the Vilcha border point in the Kiev region, 50 kilometers from the border with Belarus, the Ukrainian Border Service reported. "Russian troops violated the state border. The enemy's war equipment crossed through the Vilcha border point," the entity reported, according to which the Ukrainian Army put up a battle with the Russian Army.

12:40 NATO activates its "defense plans".

Europe is facing a new security reality after Russia's invasion of Ukraine, NATO Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg said as he confirmed the alliance's decision to activate defense plans aimed at strengthening the defense of member countries in Eastern Europe. "It will be a new Europe after the invasion we saw today," Stoltenberg told a news conference after an emergency meeting of NATO ministers in Brussels.

Stoltenberg said Russia had been planning a "cold-blooded" invasion while NATO sought a diplomatic solution to the Ukraine crisis and warned that Russia's attack on Ukraine will affect Moscow's relationship with the alliance. "We have no plans to send NATO troops to Ukraine," the official confirmed in Brussels.

12:38 Turkey condemns Russian attack as "a threat to the world."

The Turkish government has condemned the Russian invasion of Ukraine as an "unacceptable violation of international law" and a threat to the security of the world. After concluding a session of the Turkish security council, chaired by President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, the presidency issued a statement calling the attack "unacceptable" and assuring that Turkey will maintain its support for Ukraine's territorial integrity, sovereignty and political unity.

A Foreign Ministry statement also called the invasion "a violation of international law," a "serious threat to the security of the region and the world" and urged Russia to "put an end to this illegal and unjust act as soon as possible."

12:35 Ukrainian President compares Russia to "Nazi Germany".

Ukrainian President Volodimir Zelensky compared the Russian invasion against his country to the actions of "Nazi Germany" during World War II in an appearance broadcast via social networks. "Russia attacked Ukraine in a cowardly and suicidal way, just like Nazi Germany did during World War II," he stated. He also urged Russian citizens to "go out" on the streets to "protest against the war." The Russian president had accused the Kiev government of neo-Nazism in the speech in which he announced the attack.

12:22 Moscow: military operation will last as long as it takes

The Kremlin affirmed that the military operation launched against Ukraine will last as long as necessary, depending on its "results" and "relevance", estimating that the Russians will support such an offensive. Russian presidential spokesman Dmitry Peskov told journalists that Moscow's goal is to impose a "neutral status" in Ukraine, a demilitarization and the elimination of "Nazis" in the country.

12:19 Costa: NATO will not intervene, but will have "deterrent" role.

"NATO will not intervene or act in Ukraine," but will act with a "deterrent" role in neighboring coalition partner countries, said Portuguese Prime Minister António Costa in his first public speech after meeting with the foreign and defense ministers. Costa "vehemently" condemned the Russian offensive and recalled that Portugal is a member of NATO's rapid reaction group this year and affirmed that Portuguese forces are prepared to place themselves under NATO's orders in "these deterrence missions".

In addition, Costa opened Portugal's doors to Ukrainian citizens leaving the country and announced that instructions have been given to the Portuguese embassies in Ukraine and neighboring countries to speed up the issuance of visas and expedite evacuation processes.

12:13 NATO to hold virtual summit on Friday

The leaders of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) will hold a summit via videoconference tomorrow, Friday, to discuss the military actions initiated by Russia in Ukraine, diplomatic sources said Thursday (24.02.2022).

Meanwhile, NATO announced today in a statement that its member states had decided to take "additional steps" to strengthen "defense across the alliance." "Our measures are preventive, proportionate, and not scalable," the text notes.

12:01 Olaf Scholz: "This is Putin's war."

"There is no justification. This is Putin's war," German Chancellor Olaf Scholz said at an appearance in Berlin in which he again stressed that the Russian president is "flagrantly violating international law." Scholz joined London and Paris in calling for a NATO summit.

The chancellor advanced that "as a next step" NATO and European Union (EU) partners will decide on a package of "tougher" sanctions with which to make it clear to Moscow that it will pay "a bitter price" for the aggression.

11:55 Macron calls for NATO meeting.

French President Emmanuel Macron called for a NATO summit "as soon as possible" in the wake of the Russian offensive in Ukraine, his office said. The president "wishes the holding of a NATO summit as soon as possible, in concert with our partners and allies," the Elysée said, following a similar request from British Prime Minister Boris Johnson.

11:45 Lithuania to impose state of emergency after Russian invasion of Ukraine

Lithuania, an EU and NATO member country, declared that it is going to impose a state of emergency on its territory. "Today I am going to sign a decree to impose a state of emergency," declared Lithuanian President Gitanas Nauseda after a meeting of the National Defense Council.

He also indicated that the country will request the activation of "NATO Article IV", which allows for emergency consultations if a member of the military alliance is under threat, as other countries have already announced. The ambassadors of NATO's 30 member countries are scheduled to hold an emergency meeting on Thursday, a spokesman for the military alliance announced, although more and more voices are calling for a summit of leaders.

11:26 Germany offers to help with refugees from Ukraine

German Interior Minister Nancy Faeser offered support to Eastern European countries, especially Poland, in the face of the expected wave of Ukrainian refugees. The German press estimates that between two hundred thousand and one million people could arrive in the European Union from Ukraine. "We will offer massive help to the affected countries, especially to our neighbor Poland, if there are strong movements of refugees," he said in a statement.

Read: Ukraine closes its airspace to civilian flights

Also the governor of Berlin, Franziska Giffey, told local television that the city is preparing for the arrival of refugees. "For the next week, we have set ourselves the goal to discuss concrete implications, what preparations we can make, especially in case people flee this situation," Giffey told rbb.

11:22 Ukrainian refugees cross the border to Moldova

About two thousand Ukrainian refugees already crossed the border with Moldova after the beginning of the Russian military operation, Moldovan Interior Minister Anda Revenko reported. "So far we have registered about 1,900 Ukrainian citizens who have crossed the Moldovan border. There are even whole families. Five people applied for asylum," he informed at a press conference, quoted by the Russian agency TASS.

For her part, Moldovan President Maia Sandu assured that her country "will take care" of the refugees and noted an increase in the migration flow at the border crossing points with Ukraine. "We will help people who need our help. At the moment we are ready to receive tens of thousands of people," he added.

11:18 United Kingdom calls for emergency NATO meeting.

British Prime Minister Boris Johnson on Thursday called for an urgent meeting of leaders of NATO member countries in response to Russia's invasion of Ukraine, which he called a "catastrophe" for Europe. "I call for an urgent meeting of all NATO leaders as soon as possible," Johnson tweeted, adding that he will address a speech to Britons during the day.

11:18 Ukrainian casualty toll rises: 40 soldiers, 10 civilians

More than 40 Ukrainian soldiers and a dozen civilians were killed in the first hours of the invasion launched by Russia against the neighboring country, an adviser to the Ukrainian presidency said. "I know that more than 40 servicemen were killed and several dozens were wounded. There are also about ten civilians killed," Oleksiy Arestovich told reporters.

Read: Russia defends its attack in Ukraine, says it is not seeking occupation

11:05 Moscow says pro-Russian separatists are gaining territory.

The Russian Army announced that the pro-Russian separatists in eastern Ukraine it supports are making territorial gains against the Ukrainian army. General Igor Konashenkov, spokesman for the Russian Defense Ministry, said in statements to television that the rebels advanced three kilometers in the Donetsk region and one and a half kilometers in Lugansk, and assured that civilians had "nothing to fear" because Russia has only military objectives.

10:43 Ukraine breaks off diplomatic relations with Russia

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced that his country breaks diplomatic relations with Russia after the military aggression against Ukrainian territory ordered by the head of the Kremlin, Vladimir Putin.

10:34 Navalni says he is "against this war".

Russian opposition leader Alexei Navalni, who is imprisoned and faces new charges, expressed his opposition to the attack launched by Moscow, which "will cause a large number of casualties, ruin lives and continue the policy of impoverishment of Russian citizens."

"I am against this war. I believe that this war between Russia and Ukraine is being waged to cover up the robbery of Russian citizens and divert their attention from the problems inside the country, from the deterioration of the economy," he said at a hearing of the retrial opened against him last week, according to a video posted by the opposition Dojd channel.

10:23 Slovakia will also ask NATO to activate its Article 4.

Slovakia, which shares a 97-kilometer border with Ukraine, will ask today at the urgent meeting of the North Atlantic Council to open consultations on Article 4 of the treaty, which applies when one of the alliance countries feels threatened. "The situation demands it," said Foreign Minister Ivan Korcok.

In addition to Slovakia, the governments of Poland and the Baltic countries Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia also appealed to NATO's Article 4, which provides for immediate consultations among allies, while warning against the "foreseeable" Russian disinformation campaign and cyberattacks.

10:23 Berlin calls for a strong reaction from the G7, Europe and NATO.

"We will coordinate, within the EU, NATO and the G7, to implement the toughest sanctions package," German Foreign Minister Annalena Baerbock said, warning that these punitive measures will hit the German economy.

This war in our neighborhood will have repercussions for us, such as rising prices or falls in the stock markets," she admitted. "But if we do not react with fortitude, the price will be even higher," he added in a formal statement without questions.

Baerbock today chaired a virtual conference of G7 foreign ministers - which Germany chairs this year - at which, according to a ministry press release, all members condemned the Russian attack. A meeting of the group's leaders is scheduled for this afternoon.

Read: Biden accuses Putin of unjustified attack on Ukraine

10:19 Ukraine calls volunteer reservists to arms.

Kiev has issued a call to arms to volunteers of the Territorial Defense Units. "Ukraine has entered full defense mode. Anyone who is ready and able to hold a weapon can join the Territorial Defense Units in their region," this military formation announced on its Facebook page, while giving a list of addresses of all recruitment centers in the country.

10:17 Council of Europe condemns attack and announces measures

The Secretary General of the Council of Europe, Marija Pejcinovic Buric, condemned the Russian attack on Ukraine, "a flagrant violation of the Statute" of that body, while announcing a meeting of its bodies to "respond to the current situation".

"This is a dark hour for Europe and everything it stands for," Pejcinovic said in a statement, in which he pointed out that the armed action is also a violation of the European Convention on Human Rights.

10:06 Hundreds of Ukrainians cross the border to take refuge in Romania.

"Several hundreds" of Ukrainian citizens crossed in the early hours of Thursday the border separating their country from Romania (over 600 km long) to seek refuge in homes of friends and relatives in the face of the large-scale military invasion activated by Russia, Romanian authorities reported.

"The first data from the Border Police show an increase of several hundred people, although many of them have Romanian nationality, relatives or friends and even their own homes in Suceava," the prefect of this Romanian province bordering Ukraine told G4Media.

According to some estimates, the Romanian minority in Ukraine numbers about 400,000 people. Romania's Defense Minister Vasile Dincu told the media this week that his government is ready to take in more than half a million refugees from Ukraine.

09:57 Russian stock market opens with a 45.2% drop

The Russian stock market resumed trading after a temporary halt following the announcement about the start of a Russian military operation in Ukraine with the MOEX index currently down 45.2%. This morning, the Russian MOEX stock index suspended all trading on the trading floor until further notice. European stock exchanges also opened with declines of around 4%.

09:49 Belarus does not take part in the Russian military operation

Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko said that his country's troops are not taking part in the "special military operation" launched by Russia in Ukraine. "Today I read: 'About 05.00 a.m. the Ukrainian border in sector of Russia and Belarus was attacked by Russian troops, supported by Belarus.' You scoundrels! Our troops have no participation in this operation," the head of state said at a meeting with military personnel, quoted by the official BELTA agency.

09:39 Ukraine denounces entry of Russian tank columns into Lugansk

The Ukrainian Interior Ministry denounced the entry of several columns of Russian tanks into the area of the Kiev-controlled Lugansk region in the east of the country. "Russian tank columns entered the Lugansk region near the villages of Krasna Talivka, Milove, Horodysche," the Ministry states on its Facebook page.

09:32 Russia assures that it does not attack Ukrainian cities.

"The Russian Armed Forces do not attack Ukrainian cities. There is no threat to the peaceful population," the Russian Defense Ministry said in a statement. The Russian military indicated that high-precision weapons are used against Ukrainian military infrastructure, anti-aircraft batteries and air bases.

"According to intelligence data, units and servicemen of the Ukrainian Armed Forces leavemassively their positions indicated Defense, which stressed that the places where the Ukrainian forces have laid down their arms are not subjected to attacks. He added that the statements of the Ukrainian side about the losses of aircraft and armored vehicles by the Russian army are a "complete lie".

09:28 Ukrainian order to inflict "maximum casualties" on Russian forces.

"The supreme commander of the armed forces [President Volodimir Zelensky] has ordered to inflict maximum casualties on the aggressor," said Ukrainian armed forces commanding general Valery Zaluzhni, assuring that the army was "countering with dignity" the enemy's attacks.

09:20 Ukraine claims to have recaptured town in Lugansk and killed 50 Russian troops

The Ukrainian Center for Strategic Communications and Information Security assured that the Ukrainian Army recaptured the town of Shchastia in the Lugansk region, and annihilated 50 Russian troops. "Shchastia is in our power!" the entity announced on its Facebook account.

09:17 Von der leyen condemns the "barbaric" attack and announces further sanctions.

European Commission President Ursula Von der Leyen condemned Russia's "barbaric attack" on Ukraine, announced new European sanctions against Russian "strategic sectors," including blocking its banks from the European market, and warned Moscow that the European Union will not allow it to "tear down the security architecture" on the continent.

"Once again, in the heart of Europe innocent women and men are suffering. We condemn this barbaric attack and the cynical argument to justify it," Von der Leyen said in a statement to the press alongside the European Union's high representative for foreign policy, Josep Borrell.

"We are in Europe's darkest hours since World War II," said Borrell, for whom the sanctions package they are preparing will be the "most massive and toughest we have ever adopted" and warned Russian President Vladimir Putin that if he does not back down Russia will be "subjected to unprecedented isolation."

09:14 Poland asks to activate NATO Article 4

The government in Warsaw called for activating Article 4 of the NATO treaty, which provides for consultations between members "when, in the opinion of any of them, the territorial integrity, political independence or security of any of the Parties would be threatened."

"A moment ago, the (Polish) ambassador (ndlr) in Brussels submitted this request to the NATO secretary general, with a group of allies," Polish government spokesman Piotr Müller said. The ambassadors of the 30 member countries of the military alliance are due to meet urgently on Thursday in Brussels, a NATO spokesman announced.

08:50 Moscow closes sea transport between Ukraine and Russia

Russia decreed the closure of maritime traffic in the Sea of Azov, which stretches between Russia and Ukraine, following Vladimir Putin's announcement of an attack on the neighboring country, Russian agencies said. "In connection with the development of anti-terrorist activities, transportation in the Sea of Azov is suspended from 04:00 (02:00 CET) on February 24 until further notice," a representative of the federal maritime traffic agency Rosmorrechflot told Russian press agencies.

Read: Attention: Putin announces Russian military operation in Ukraine

08:48 Beijing insists on "keeping calm" despite attack.

"China is closely following the latest developments in Ukraine. We call on all parties involved to remain calm to prevent the situation from getting out of control," Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Hua Chunying told a press conference.

Hours earlier, the Chinese ambassador to the United Nations, Zhang Jun, commented before the last meeting of the Security Council that the Asian country believes that "the door to a peaceful solution of the Ukrainian crisis has not yet been completely closed". The ambassador said China's position on "safeguarding the sovereignty and territorial integrity of states" has always been "consistent," but avoided explicitly condemning the Russian attack on Ukraine.

08:46 Germany can maintain its supply without Russian gas

German Vice Chancellor and Economics Minister Robert Habeck said that Germany is in a position to secure energy supplies without Russian gas and that one cannot be energetically dependent on a country that violates international law.

"We had hoped that it would come to this situation but we knew it could happen and had taken precautions. We cannot be so dependent on a country that violates international law. We are in a position to maintain supply," Habeck told German television.

Habeck also referred to the status of the Nord Stream II pipeline - which should transport gas from Russia to Germany via the Baltic - and said he did not see it being able to start operating in the short or medium term. However, he added that in the long term, work must be done to bring Germany back to normal relations with Russia.

08:39 France "strongly" condemns war in Ukraine.

"France strongly condemns Russia's decision to wage war on Ukraine," French President Emmanuel Macron said Thursday, calling on Moscow to "immediately end its military operations." "France stands in solidarity with Ukraine. It stands by the Ukrainians and acts with its partners and allies to stop the war," the head of state added in two tweets.

Macron spoke by telephone with the Ukrainian president, Volodimir Zelenski, who asked him for "unity" of the Europeans in the face of the Russian attack. The French president, who also spoke with the head of the European Council Charles Michel, expressed "all the support and solidarity of France," the Elysee added.

08:48 Ukraine reports at least eight dead and a dozen wounded.

"A woman and a child were injured in the Konopot region, where a car burned. In the city of Podolsk of the Odessa region, seven dead, seven wounded and 19 missing as a result of shelling. In the city of Mariupol, Donetsk region, one dead and two wounded," Interior Ministry advisor Anton Geraschenko reported on his Telegram channel.

08:39 UK orders its airlines to avoid Ukrainian airspace

The UK ordered its airlines to avoid Ukrainian airspace "to keep passengers and crew safe," Transport Minister Grant Shapps announced. The minister assured that his government "stands with the Ukrainian people and is working with our international partners to respond to this act of aggression".

British Prime Minister Boris Johnson is chairing from 08:30 CET a meeting of his emergency cabinet (COBRA) at which new sanctions against Russia and other measures are expected to be adopted.

08:32 Russia's central bankintervenes to halt the ruble's slide

Russia's central bank on Thursday announced "interventions" in the foreign exchange market to "stabilize the situation" following the start of a Russian military offensive in Ukraine, which triggered falls of up to 10% in the ruble against the dollar. In early morning trading, the ruble was already at an all-time low of 90 rubles to the dollar, down 9.02% from the previous day's close.

"The Bank of Russia will ensure the maintenance of financial stability and the continuity of operations of financial institutions, using all necessary tools," the institution said, assuring that it had "clear action plans for any scenario."

08:30 Russian troops enter Ukraine through Crimea

title: UPDATE 1-Top Russian lender Sberbank ready for anything as sanctions loom
text:
(Adds detail)

By Alexander Marrow

MOSCOW, Feb 24 (Reuters) - Russia's largest lender Sberbank said on Thursday that it was prepared for any developments as the threat of sanctions grew after Russian forces attacked Ukraine, sending shares in Russian banks crashing.

Russian forces invaded Ukraine by land, air and sea on Thursday, confirming the worst fears of the West with the biggest attack by one state against another in Europe since World War Two.

A senior U.S. administration official told reporters on Tuesday that Sberbank and No. 2 lender VTB would face U.S. sanctions if Moscow proceeded with its invasion of Ukraine, warning that no Russian financial institutions were safe.

"We are prepared for any development of the situation and have worked through scenarios for guaranteeing that our customers funds, assets and interests are protected, and also that our functions are fully operational," Sberbank said on Thursday.

VTB said its branches, ATMs and online services were functioning normally.

Both banks previously declined to comment on potential sanctions.

Moscow-listed shares of both banks underperformed the wider market, which had lost around 33%. Sberbank shares were down 49.4% as of 1132 GMT - its lowest in six years, while VTB shares dropped 41.3%, earlier hitting an all-time low.

Online bank Tinkoff, whose London-listed shares fell 45.2%, said its systems were running smoothly.

"Tinkoff has sufficient liquidity," the bank, which is not state-owned, but is listed by the central bank as one of 13 systemically important banks in Russia, said.

"We are seeing increased demand for cash withdrawals and are replenishing ATMs on a reinforced schedule."

The rouble bounced off all-time lows on Thursday as the central bank announced FX interventions after President Vladimir Putin ordered Russian forces to invade Ukraine, a move expected to trigger new harsh sanctions against Moscow.

(Reporting by Alexander Marrow and Elena Fabrichnaya; Editing by Katya Golubkova and Kim Coghill and Elaine Hardcastle)

title: Russian stock exchange resumes trading with a 45.2% drop
text:
The Moscow Stock Exchange resumed trading after the temporary pause following President Vladimir Putin's announcement on the start of military intervention in Ukraine, which began with a 45.2% plunge according to an official statement.

On Thursday morning the Moscow Stock Exchange reported a temporary suspension of all its trading on the trading floor until further notice.

The Moscow Stock Exchange has suspended trading on all its markets until further notice," the exchange's management said in a brief statement.

The stock exchange had closed the previous session with a drop of 1.84%.

The stocks that fell the most at the resumption of the Stock Exchange were Rosneft(58.5 %, EN+ (58.3 %) and Sberbank (57 %).

Measures to stabilize the financial market Due to the military tensions between Russia and Ukraine in recent weeks, the MOEXindex lost 52.13 % in the last month and 55.37 % in the last year.

The Bank of Russia will ensure financial stability and uninterrupted continuity of operations of financial organizations," the Russian monetary institution said in a statement.

The Russian currency today surpassed the mark of almost 90 rubles to the dollar and 101 to the euro for Russian actions in Ukraine.

Sber guaranteed interest protection The fall of the Russian currency and stocks began on February 21, after the announcement about Moscow'srecognition of the separatist republics of Donbas.
